result.stdout:
etamil 2.0.0 — the eTamil compiler

USAGE:
    etamil [OPTIONS] <FILE>
    cat program.qmz | etamil [OPTIONS]

OPTIONS:
    --vm               Run on the bytecode VM (default)
    --check            Lex, parse and type check only — never runs the program
    --repl             Interactive shell: type an expression, see what it comes to
    --server           Start the synchronous HTTP server
    --async            Concurrent server: async accept, blocking handlers
                       இடைவெளி blocks run on a timer under either server
    --llvm             LLVM backend (requires --features llvm; Linux/macOS)
    --llvm-gaps        List what the LLVM backend would refuse — no LLVM needed
    --artino           Compile for an Arduino board (requires --features llvm)
    --board <BOARD>    With --artino: uno (default), nano, mega, pico, pico2;
                       host builds an object for this machine, for testing
    --out <DIR>        With --artino: where the sketch goes (default: artino-build)
    --upload <PORT>    With --artino: build and upload through arduino-cli
    --artino-gaps      List what --artino would refuse — no LLVM needed
    --host <HOST>      Server bind address (default: 127.0.0.1)
    --port <PORT>      Server port (default: 8080)
    -h, --help         Show this message
    -V, --version      Show the version

EXAMPLES:
    etamil --vm program.qmz
    echo "950000" | etamil --vm examples/basic_samples/example.qmz
    etamil --server --port 8080 examples/backend/hello_server.qmz
    cat program.qmz | etamil --check     # errors only, nothing runs
    etamil --repl                        # try something without a file
    etamil --llvm-gaps nUlakam/paNam/kAcu.qmz  # what stops --llvm compiling it
    etamil --artino --board uno blink.qmz  # a sketch folder for arduino-cli
